title: "Architecture & IPC Contract"
format: html

This document explains the internal architecture of RDesk, the native process pipeline, and the JSON IPC communication protocol.

## System Architecture

Unlike web-based frameworks that require a local HTTP server and WebSocket daemon listening on loopback TCP ports, RDesk operates entirely over operating system process pipes.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    subgraph UI ["Embedded Frontend (WebView2)"]
        HTML["HTML5 / DOM"]
        JS["rdesk.js Bridge"]
    end

    subgraph NativeBridge ["Native C++ Window Bridge"]
        WV2["Microsoft Edge WebView2"]
        Launcher["rdesk-launcher.exe"]
    end

    subgraph RSession ["R Backend Process"]
        App["RDesk::App (Event Loop)"]
        Handlers["Registered Message Handlers"]
        WorkerPool["Background Workers (callr / mirai)"]
    end

    HTML --> JS
    JS -- "window.chrome.webview.postMessage" --> WV2
    WV2 --> Launcher
    Launcher -- "Standard I/O Pipes (stdin/stdout)" --> App
    App --> Handlers
    Handlers -. "Async Dispatch" .-> WorkerPool
    WorkerPool -. "Return Payload" .-> App
    App -- "Standard Output (JSON Envelope)" --> Launcher
    Launcher -- "ExecuteScript(rdesk._dispatch)" --> WV2
    WV2 --> JS
    JS --> HTML
```

### Key Architectural Layers

1. **Native Window Host (`rdesk-launcher.exe`)**:
   * A lightweight C++ application built on Windows API and Microsoft Edge WebView2.
   * Hosts the WebView2 browser control and initializes the native window chrome.
   * Captures standard input from the R process and forwards standard output back to R.
2. **R Controller Process (`RDesk::App`)**:
   * Spawns `rdesk-launcher.exe` as a child process using `processx`.
   * Manages an event-driven message loop reading non-blocking JSON envelopes.
   * Dispatches events to registered R callbacks.
3. **Async Compute Workers**:
   * CPU-intensive tasks run in separate background processes via `callr` or `mirai`.
   * The main R event loop remains unblocked and responsive to user input.

::: {.callout-important}
## Security Advantages of Pure Pipe IPC
Because no TCP or UDP ports are opened, an RDesk application is invisible to local port scanners, firewall rules, and browser security policies. Local files are served through virtual host mapping (`https://rdesk.local/`) rather than an insecure `http://localhost` origin.
:::

## IPC Message Protocol

Every message sent across the pipe is a single line containing a JSON object conforming to the RDesk Envelope Protocol.

### Message Schema

```json
{
  "id": "msg_12345",
  "event": "filter_data",
  "payload": {
    "column": "cyl",
    "value": "6"
  },
  "timestamp": 1788416688
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `id` | String | Unique monotonically increasing identifier for tracing requests. |
| `event` | String | Name of the event or handler to invoke. |
| `payload` | Object | Arbitrary data passed between frontend and backend. |
| `timestamp` | Number | Unix epoch timestamp (seconds). |

### Bidirectional Flow

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    participant JS as JavaScript (rdesk.js)
    participant Pipe as OS Named Pipe
    participant R as R Engine (App)

    Note over JS,R: 1. Frontend requests action
    JS->>Pipe: {"event": "calculate", "payload": {"n": 1000}}
    Pipe->>R: Read line from stdin
    Note over R: Execute R callback
    R->>Pipe: {"event": "calculate_result", "payload": {"result": 42}}
    Pipe->>JS: Dispatch event to JS listener
    Note over JS: Update DOM
```

## Window Bridging (`rdesk_open_window()`)

For multi-window workflows or opening external dialogs, RDesk provides native window control:

```r
# Open secondary inspection window
win <- RDesk:::rdesk_open_window(
  url    = "https://rdesk.local/inspector.html",
  title  = "Data Inspector",
  width  = 900L,
  height = 600L
)
```

The native window lifecycle is monitored by `processx`: when the window is closed, the process terminates gracefully and R releases allocated resources.
